proposal: The Mandate recommends that, wherever responsibility for the Strategic Petroleum Reserve sits, the Department of Energy ensure the reserve is maintained for national strategic purposes and not misused for political gain. The task here covers the reserve's upkeep and the stated basis for any use.
remaining: Return of exchanged barrels and refill toward capacity (the reserve held just over 400 million barrels of its 700 million-barrel capacity in October 2025, per DOE)
A stated policy limiting use to strategic purposes rather than price management (page 377)

flags: Stage moved from diverged 0 to in_progress 30 because the 2026 releases were part of a coordinated IEA collective action during an Iran-related supply disruption, were structured as exchanges returning premium barrels, and were preceded by a funded refill purchase; the price rationale is one of several stated aims.

Judgment call: diverged 0 would also be defensible, because DOE's primary March 2026 statement names lowering energy prices as an aim of the release and the reserve reached a multi-decade low; proposed would be defensible if the refill is judged too small to count.
Removed related id c06-06 (Iran sanctions), which does not overlap the reserve recommendation.

status_summary: On 2025-10-21 DOE issued a solicitation to buy one million barrels for the reserve, citing $171 million appropriated to begin refilling it and restore it to full operational capacity. On 2026-03-11 DOE announced release of 172 million barrels as its share of a coordinated 400 million-barrel International Energy Agency action, stating the aim of lowering energy prices and citing threats to energy security from Iran and its proxies, with about 200 million barrels to be returned within a year. On 2026-09-29 DOE issued a request for an exchange of up to 40 million barrels under that commitment, describing it as addressing short-term supply disruptions and providing for return of the barrels plus premium barrels to raise long-term inventory.

timeline.event: DOE issued a solicitation to purchase one million barrels of crude oil for the Bryan Mound site, citing $171 million appropriated to begin refilling the reserve.

DOE announced the release of 172 million barrels from the reserve as the U.S. share of a coordinated 400 million-barrel International Energy Agency action, citing lower energy prices and threats to energy security from Iran and its proxies, with about 200 million barrels to be returned within a year.

DOE issued a request for proposals for an exchange of up to 40 million barrels from the Big Hill and Bryan Mound sites under the 172 million-barrel commitment, citing short-term supply disruptions, with borrowed barrels returned plus premium barrels; bids were due 2026-10-06.

title: Keep the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for strategic purposes, not political price ends
uncertainties: Stage reflects a judgment. The Mandate asks that the reserve be maintained for national strategic purposes and not misused for political gain. DOE's March 2026 statement names lowering energy prices as an aim alongside Iran-related energy security threats, while its September 2026 statement describes the releases as an IEA response to short-term supply disruptions structured as exchanges that add premium barrels. A trade report states the reserve fell to its lowest level since 1982 and that returns run to late 2028; this was not reconciled against EIA inventory data. Searches run on energy.gov and trade news.
